primary_diagnosis.environmental_trigger: Extremely high humidity (96%), moderate temperature (22.4 °C), and wet canopy conditions favoring fungal spore germination and secondary spread.

chemical_control.dosage: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.0-2.5 g/L of water or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2.0 g/L of water.
chemical_control.spray_guidelines: Apply as a protective foliar spray ensuring thorough coverage of both upper and lower leaf surfaces. Repeat at 7-10 day intervals during persistent high humidity.
chemical_control.pre_harvest_interval: 7 to 14 days depending on specific active ingredient used.

biological_control.application_frequency: Every 5 to 7 days during high relative humidity or at first sign of disease onset.
biological_control.application_procedure: Foliar spray applied early in the morning or late afternoon to avoid leaf scorch, thoroughly wetting the canopy.

cultural_remediation.irrigation_adjustments: Maintain drip irrigation to avoid leaf wetness; ensure irrigation runs early in the day so any accidental splash dries rapidly.
cultural_remediation.field_sanitation: Prune and destroy infected lower leaves showing lesions; clear and burn infected plant debris post-harvest; maintain a 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
cultural_remediation.soil_drainage_and_aeration: Improve field air circulation by proper plant spacing, staking/trellising plants, and pruning lower leaves up to 30 cm from the soil surface.

recovery_followup.monitoring_milestones: Inspect lower to mid-canopy leaves every 3-4 days for new lesion development; verify leaf drying efficiency after irrigation.
recovery_followup.secondary_treatment_conditions: If lesions continue spreading into the upper canopy or if high humidity (>90%) persists past 7 days, rotate to a systemic fungicide like Azoxystrobin.
